LESSON: PHONIC DEVELOPMENT

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: READING
Topic 3.2: Phonic development

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Phonic development. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read and sound syllables  Learners blend and segment sounds to build

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PHONIC DEVELOPMENT
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Phonic development helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: PHONIC DEVELOPMENT
Study Phonic development like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Read and sound syllables  Learners blend and segment sounds to build

What this means
In this part you learn to read and sound syllables  Learners blend and segment sounds to build. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read and sound syllables  Learners blend and segment sounds to build.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Phonic development”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read and sound syllables  Learners blend and segment sounds to build. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Phonic development is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Phonic development”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read and sound syllables  Learners blend and segment sounds to build)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Phonic development to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read and sound syllables  Learners blend and segment sounds to build.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Phonic development from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Phonic development: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Phonic development?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Phonic development means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read and sound syllables  Learners blend and segment sounds to build.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
